title: Marshmallow Swirl Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Half-yolk vanilla custard with a homemade egg-white marshmallow (Italian meringue) swirl folded through.
summary: Our classic vanilla custard made lighter with four yolks, then swirled with homemade, gelatine-free marshmallow whipped from egg whites and hot syrup. Soft, sweet ribbons run through every scoop.
equipment: stand mixer or electric hand whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
large egg whites, at room temperature (pasteurised if needed)
liquid glucose or light corn syrup

steps.title: Infuse the dairy
steps.text: Bring the milk and cream just to the boil, stir in the 2 tsp vanilla and leave off the heat for 30 min.

steps.title: Make the custard
steps.text: Whisk the yolks, 100 g sugar and salt until pale, whisk in the warm dairy and pour it back into the pan.

steps.title: Cook and chill
steps.text: Stir over low heat to 77-80 °C, when it should coat the spatula. Strain, cool in the iced water and chill for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Boil the syrup
steps.text: Heat the water, 75 g sugar and glucose in the small saucepan with the sugar thermometer clipped on. Do not stir once it boils.

steps.title: Whip the whites
steps.text: When the syrup reaches 107 °C, start whisking the egg whites and cream of tartar to soft peaks.

steps.title: Make the marshmallow
steps.text: At 115 °C, pour the syrup in a thin stream down the inside of the bowl with the mixer on medium-low. Whisk on high for 7-8 min until thick, glossy and cool, then beat in the 1/2 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Churn and swirl
steps.text: Churn the custard until thick but still soft. Fold in the marshmallow with just a few strokes so it stays in streaks, then freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Pour the syrup against the bowl, not onto the whisk, or it will spin into threads.
A common mistake is over-folding; the swirl disappears into the ice cream.
The marshmallow keeps for a day at room temperature in a sealed container if you make it ahead.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
